note: Part B (Q58-59, drawing, 100 marks) is not transcribed: no model answer exists (brochure 17.2).

questions.text: How many times does the most used black coloured shape appear in the composition shown below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The 40 black shapes (5 rows of 8) come in three kinds of cross: a plain plus with sharp inner corners and flat arm ends, a plus with softly rounded inner corners, and a fully rounded blob-like cross. Sort them row by row: the sharp plus appears 3, 3, 2, 3 and 3 times in the five rows, 14 in all. Each of the two rounded kinds appears 13 times, so the most used shape appears 14 times.

questions.text: In the image shown below, PQ = QR = QS = 2 units. Also, QT = TS = QU = UR. The points T and U are the centre points of the semicircles. What is the total area of shaded portions in square units?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Put Q at the origin, so P = (-2, 0), R = (2, 0), S = (0, 2); triangles PQS and QRS each have area 2. The semicircle on QS (centre T, radius 1) meets PS at (-1, 1), so the part of it outside the triangle is a 90 degree segment of area \(\pi/4 - 1/2\). The part of triangle PQS outside the semicircle is \(2 - (\pi/2 - (\pi/4 - 1/2)) = 3/2 - \pi/4\). These two shaded pieces add to exactly 1, and the right side (semicircle on QR, centre U) works the same way, so the total shaded area is 2 square units.

questions.text: What is the number that you get when you divide the difference between the number of triangles and number of circles by the number of rectangles for the image shown below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count the full circles: the left circle, the small bottom circle and the big circle make 3 (the open arc at the top right is not a circle). Count the rectangles on the right block: the upper one, the lower one and the two together make 3. Count every triangle formed by straight lines: 4 in the left arrow-shaped block, 5 in the arrowhead group inside the left circle (the big arrow, the small arrow and three pieces between them), 1 inside the big circle and 11 in the lower right rectangle with its crossing diagonals, 21 in all. Then (21 minus 3) divided by 3 = 6.

questions.text: Shown below is the front and top views of two cubes. The red and blue cubes are made up of metal and wax respectively. Red cube is heated and is hot enough to melt wax in the blue cube. As shown in the front and top views, the red cube is moved along the path PQRS creating sharp edges and flat surfaces on the blue cube. What is the total number of surfaces the blue cube will have after the red cube reaches the point S?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The hot cube's top is level with the wax cube's top, so it melts an open groove of square section that runs in from the left face (P to Q), turns diagonally (Q to R) and runs out through the right face (R to S). In the top view the groove has 8 straight side walls: 4 on the back side (along PQ, the end of Q, the diagonal, along RS) and 4 on the front side (along PQ, the diagonal, the end of R, along RS), plus 1 flat floor. The groove splits the top face into 2 separate pieces, and the left, right, front, back and bottom faces remain, so the total is 8 + 1 + 2 + 5 = 16 surfaces.

questions.text: One of the pots does not belong to the group of pots shown below. What is the number written on that pot?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Look at which side each pot leaks from. Every pot with an even number (34, 18, 26, 22, 54, 22) leaks on the left, and every pot with an odd number (57, 43, 51, 15, 75, 81, 73, 45, 37) leaks on the right. The pot numbered 62 is even but leaks on the right, so it does not belong.

questions.text: What is the number of different patterns on the capsules shown below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Every capsule is half black and half patterned, so compare only the patterned halves relative to the capsule's own length. There are lines running along the capsule, lines running across it, a brick pattern with lines across and short dashes, and a ladder-like brick pattern with lines along and short dashes. No other pattern appears, so there are 4 different patterns.

questions.text: A composition made of letters is shown below. What is the total number of letters used to create this image?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Read the picture part by part. The cat uses A, A (ears), S, S, D, D (glasses), D (nose), d and k (rotated, left side), U, a large S and an L (leg and base), O (body), Y, 1, E and o inside the body, y (tail) and two D wheels: 20 letters. The garden tools use a D (base), four U shapes (fork heads), a Y joining two of them, three long I strokes for the handles and two J hooks: 11 letters. That is 31 letters in all.

questions.text: A sharpened pencil with eraser is shown in image P. How many sharpened pencils with erasers are in image Q?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Follow each of the 19 pencils in Q from one end to the other and note what is at each end. A pencil counts only if it has a sharpened tip at one end and an eraser at the other, like P. Eight pencils have both; the rest have a sharpened tip with a plain cut end (5) or an eraser with a plain cut end (4). So 8 pencils match P.

questions.text: Several kettles are shown below. What is the total number of usable kettles that are designed to store and pour hot water?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A kettle can only pour if its spout is on the side opposite the handle and near the top. Of the 17 kettles, four fail: the jug with a window in the top row has its spout above the handle, and three electric kettles (one in the middle row, two in the bottom row) have the spout tucked under or below the handle near the base. The remaining 13 kettles are usable.

questions.text: Given below are 8 triangular pieces of a puzzle made from the shape P. What is the three-digit number formed when these pieces are arranged correctly?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each piece is a right-angled triangle from P, with its right angle at the middle of a side of the square and its two sharp corners at the centre and at a corner of the square. The black marks on every piece sit near one sharp corner, so that corner goes to the centre of P. Turning the pieces so the cut strokes line up across the joins gives the digits 7, 4 and 5 written across the middle, so the number is 745.

questions.text: Given below is a drawing on a sheet of paper. Make a cut along the solid arcs and fold the resulting semicircular rings at 90 degrees along the dotted lines. What is the number of raised semicircular rings after following these steps?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Number the bands between neighbouring arcs from the inside out. A band rises only where it is cut free along both curved edges and has fold lines at both ends lying on one straight line. The 2nd and 4th bands from the inside are upper semicircles with dotted lines at both ends on the horizontal line, and the 1st, 3rd and 5th bands are right-hand semicircles with dotted lines at both ends on the vertical line. That gives 2 + 3 = 5 raised semicircular rings; the inner half-disc also lifts but it is not a ring.

questions.text: A mobile screen has a dimension of 10 cm x 4 cm (height x width). A mobile user is viewing a picture in portrait mode and it occupies the entire screen. The user rotates the screen to landscape mode. After rotation, the height of the picture is now the width of the screen and its width gets reduced proportionately, leaving equal blank spaces on both sides of the picture. What is the area (in square centimeters) of the blank space on the left-hand side of the picture?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: In landscape the screen is 4 cm tall and 10 cm wide. The 10 cm tall picture must shrink to a height of 4 cm, so its width shrinks in the same ratio from 4 cm to 4 x 4/10 = 1.6 cm. The blank width is 10 minus 1.6 = 8.4 cm, split equally, so each side is 4.2 cm wide and 4 cm tall. Area on the left = 4.2 x 4 = 16.8 square cm.

questions.text: What number will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Add each number to the number in the opposite triangle across the centre: 43 + 26 = 69, 31 + 38 = 69 and 40 + 29 = 69. So 35 and the missing number must also add to 69, giving 69 minus 35 = 34.

questions.text: A tank with internal dimension 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm (length x width x height) is fully filled with spherical marbles, each marble having a diameter of 1 cm. Each layer of marbles should have equal number of marbles. Water is then poured into the tank. What is the volume of water in cubic centimeters required to fill the voids? (Use π=22/7)
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Equal layers of 1 cm marbles in a 10 cm cube give 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 marbles. Each marble has volume \((4/3)\pi(0.5)^3 = 11/21\) cubic cm with \(\pi = 22/7\), so the marbles fill 11000/21, about 523.81 cubic cm. Water fills the rest: 1000 minus 523.81 = 476.19 cubic cm.

questions.text: Image P shows an object as seen from the top. Which of the objects given below will appear as shown in image P when viewed from the top? Consider all the objects are made with opaque solids.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: From the top, P shows two plain circles of the same size joined by a straight rod whose rounded ends sit inside the circles. A, B and C all look like this from above: in A the arched rod drops into the flat-topped hemisphere and the cylinder; in B the bent rod ends right above the wide top of the upside-down cone, so only one circle shows; in C the flat bar lies across the two discs and the narrower block under the right disc is hidden by it. D fails: its cone stands on its wide base, so from above it shows two circles, its base and its small top. So A, B and C.

questions.text: Q, R, S and T are cut-out shapes used to create a composition shown in image P. These cut-out shapes could be rotated and combined without overlapping to create the composition. These cut-out shapes can also be repeated. What is/are the correct combination(s) that can be used to create the composition shown in image P?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Take X as one unit. Areas: Q = 1.5, R = 1, S = 0.5, T = 2, and P = a 4 by 2 rectangle (8) minus the V notch (1) plus the triangle below (2) = 9. A adds to 7.5 and D to 10, so they fail. B (3 + 1 + 1 + 4 = 9) works: one T is the bottom triangle, two S fill the two corners beside the notch, and the other T, two Q and R fill the remaining 3 by 2 block. C (3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 9) also works: T at the bottom, two S beside the notch, each Q paired with an S into a 2 by 1 strip, and two R squares in the last column.

questions.text: Given below is a pattern P, composed of three different shapes 1, 2, and 3. Which options show the pattern(s) that is/are possible if the shape 2 is cut in half along the vertical axis, the shape 3 is rotated clockwise at the center by 45 degrees, and the shape 1 remains unchanged? Overlapping of shapes is not allowed.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Check each option for the three required changes. In all four, the black shape 1 stays upright, shape 2 appears only as a half with a straight vertical cut edge, and the grey shape 3 is turned 45 degrees clockwise (its point now at the lower left). The difference is spacing: in A, B and D every shape sits clear of its neighbours, but in C the striped halves are pushed into the black shapes so that they overlap, which the question does not allow.

questions.text: Given below are five images P, Q, R, S and T. Each of these is rotated about its center. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE? (Ignore minor variations due to pixelated appearance)

options.label: A
options.text: Patterns Q, S and T will look the same when rotated by 60°

options.label: B
options.text: Patterns Q, R and T will look the same when rotated by 120°

options.label: C
options.text: Patterns P, S and T will not look the same when rotated by 60°.

options.label: D
options.text: Patterns Q, R and T will look the same when rotated by 60° or 120°

questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Find how often each pattern repeats in one full turn: P repeats 4 times (every 90 degrees), Q 3 times (120), R has 24 equal petals (every 15 degrees), S 5 times (72) and T 3 times (120). So at 120 degrees Q, R and T all look the same, making B true. At 60 degrees P, S and T all change, making C true. A is false because Q and T do not repeat every 60 degrees, and D is false for the same reason at 60 degrees. Option D can also be read as "at 60 degrees or at 120 degrees", and Q, R and T do look the same at 120 degrees, so IIT Bombay's final key accepts both B, C and B, C, D.

questions.text: In the image below, a combination of gears (1-5), pulley (6), weight (W), belts (connecting 1&2, 4&6) and a shaft drive is shown. The shaft rotates in the direction of the arrow without any horizontal translation. Which of the following statement is /are CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: 5 rotates clockwise and W moves upwards.

options.label: B
options.text: 4 rotates anticlockwise and W moves downwards.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The arrow shows the front of the shaft moving up, and with the worm's thread slanting down to the right on the front, the thread under the shaft pushes the top teeth of gear 5 to the right, so 5 turns clockwise. Meshed gears alternate: 2 anticlockwise, 3 clockwise, 4 anticlockwise. Open belts keep the same direction, so 1 turns like 2 (anticlockwise) and pulley 6 like 4 (anticlockwise), which pulls the rope on its right side up and lifts W. So A (5 clockwise, W up) and C (5 and 4 opposite) are correct; B is wrong because W rises, and D is wrong because 1 and 4 turn the same way.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE for Ajrakh, Paithani, Kalamkari, Phulkari, Khes and Bandhani?

options.label: A
options.text: All of the above are related to textiles of India.

options.label: B
options.text: At least three of the above are painting techniques of India.

options.label: C
options.text: Three of the above are artforms from Punjab.

options.label: D
options.text: Two of the above are weaving crafts from India.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: All six are Indian textile crafts: Ajrakh (block printing), Paithani (silk weaving), Kalamkari (pen painted or block printed cloth), Phulkari (embroidery), Khes (woven cotton) and Bandhani (tie and dye), so A is true. Paithani and Khes are the two woven ones, so D is true. Only Kalamkari is a painting technique, so B is false, and only Phulkari and Khes come from Punjab, so C (three) is false.

questions.text: Which of the options is/are paintings by the artist M. F. Hussain?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: M. F. Husain is known for bold, fragmented horses, scenes from the Mahabharata and crowded compositions mixing symbols of many faiths, painted in strong colour with heavy outlines. A and B are his galloping horses (one in rich colour, one in grey), C is a Mahabharata chariot scene with Hindi lettering, and D brings together doves, a crescent, temples and Krishna in his typical style. All four carry these signature features.

questions.text: Which of the below is a/are cinema camera maker(s)?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: RED and ARRI build professional digital cinema cameras used on feature films, and Canon makes the Cinema EOS range (such as the C300 and C500) alongside its still cameras. Wacom makes graphics tablets and pen displays, not cameras.

questions.text: Which Indian city/cities is/are designated by UNESCO as a Creative City, until 2024?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Varanasi joined the UNESCO Creative Cities Network for music in 2015, and Gwalior (music) and Kozhikode (literature, India's first City of Literature) joined in 2023. Pune has not been designated.

questions.text: Shown below are Indian vehicle number plates with colour codes. Which of the option/s is/are correct?

options.label: B
options.text: P, S & U are private vehicles

options.label: C
options.text: Q, R, T & X are commercial vehicles

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: White plates with black letters (P), green plates with white letters (S, private electric) and the BH series (U) are private vehicles, so B is true. Yellow (Q), green with yellow letters (R, commercial electric) and black with yellow letters (T, self-drive rental) are commercial, so A is false. X has the upward arrow used on defence vehicles, so D is true and C is false.

questions.text: 1, 2, 3 and 4 are photographs captured using a camera with a lens set at aperture P, Q, R or S. Which of the options is/are correct?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A smaller aperture opening gives a deeper depth of field. The openings rank P (tiny) smaller than Q, then S, then R (widest). In the photos the owl is always sharp, while the front and back pots are most blurred in 1, then 2, then 4, and sharpest in 3. So P goes with 3 and R with 1 (also Q with 4 and S with 2), making A and C correct.

questions.text: Which of the following image(s) can be created by the nib type illustrated below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The nib is a broad, flat chisel nib, which makes thick and thin strokes depending on the direction of the stroke and gives flat or angled stroke ends. A (thick headline, thin uprights, square ends), B and C (thick strokes with angled ends) all show this thick and thin contrast. D has strokes of the same width everywhere with rounded ends, which needs a round nib.

questions.text: Which of these photographs follow the Rule of Thirds?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Divide each frame into thirds with two vertical and two horizontal lines. In A the boy sits on the upper right crossing, in B the seated monk is at the lower right crossing, and in C the post runs along the left third with the horizon on the lower third. In D the child is near the centre of the frame, so it does not use the rule of thirds.

questions.text: A continuous strip with a pattern is shown below. Which of the options given below is/are part of the continuous strip?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: The strip repeats the same block about four times, so slide each option along it without turning it. A and D match a section of the strip exactly. B has one small triangle drawn on the wrong side of a stroke, and C has an extra small black square that does not appear anywhere in the strip, so they are not parts of it.

questions.text: A composition made using letters from a specific font is shown below. Some letters are repeated but there is no distortion, rotation, flip or any change in orientation. Letters are used in the original form as seen in the font. Which of the following words can be formed using the letters shown in the image below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Read the overlapping letters without turning them: h at the bottom left with r above it, then s, o and g (bowl with its hooked tail at the bottom), a second s at the top right, and t in the middle. These give g, h, o, s and t for ghost, and s, h, o, r and t for short. There is no n or e in the composition, so note and enter cannot be formed.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct for a longitudinal marking provided at the centre of a road?

options.label: A
options.text: A broken longitudinal line allows overtaking.

options.label: B
options.text: A solid longitudinal line always permits overtaking.

options.label: C
options.text: Longitudinal markings are meant only for aesthetics.

options.label: D
options.text: Double solid lines may be crossed when overtaking a slow-moving vehicle.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: A broken centre line means drivers may cross it to overtake when it is safe. A solid line means do not cross, so B is wrong. Road markings guide and control traffic, they are not decoration, so C is wrong. Double solid lines must never be crossed, so D is wrong.

questions.text:
Four lines of text from a poem by E. E. Cummings is given below.

may come home with smooth round stone
as small as a world and as large as alone
for whatever we may lose (like a you or a me)
its always ourselves we find at sea

One of the four lines is depicted in the images below. Identify the image which correctly represents one line of the poem.
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Each image is a line of text printed upside down as a mirror reflection, like writing reflected in water. Flip each one top to bottom and read it. B reads 'as small as a world and as large as alone', exactly the second line of the poem. The words in A, C and D come out jumbled or mixed from different lines, so they do not represent any single line correctly.

questions.text: Samantha, Reema and Payal went late at night to visit an adventure place called The Mystery Spot. The place has a strange window-less room with white walls. One of the walls has a blue triangle and a red circle painted on it. The girls entered the room in turns. First, Samantha entered the room and came out telling that there were two shapes painted on the wall—one triangle and one circle. Then, Reema entered the same room and came out surprised as she saw only a triangle on the wall. Lastly, Payal entered the room and claimed that she saw only a circle on the wall. Which of the four statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: When Samantha entered, the room was lit by a blue light. When Reema entered the room, the light was changed to white light and when Payal entered the room, the light was changed to red.

options.label: B
options.text: When Samantha entered, the room was lit by a white light. When Reema entered the room, the light was changed to blue light and when Payal entered the room, the light was changed to red.

options.label: C
options.text: When Samantha entered, the room was lit by a white light. When Reema entered the room, the light was changed to red light and when Payal entered the room, the light was changed to blue.

options.label: D
options.text: When Samantha entered, the room was lit by a blue light. When Reema entered the room, the light was changed to red light and when Payal entered the room, the light was changed to white.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Under white light both shapes show, so Samantha saw white light. Under red light the white wall and the red circle both look red, so the circle disappears while the blue triangle looks dark: only a triangle is seen, which is what Reema saw. Under blue light the blue triangle merges with the now blue wall and the red circle looks dark: only a circle is seen, as Payal said. So the order is white, red, blue.

questions.text: Which of the options will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Track each part separately. The brackets alternate between side by side and top and bottom, so the fourth figure has them top and bottom. The shaded segment moves 3 places, then 1, then 3, then 1 around the eight segments, so it must sit on the left half of the bottom bracket. The dot moves an eighth of a turn clockwise each time, so it is at the bottom. The free circle alternates bottom left and top right, and the triangle moves clockwise from corner to corner, so both are at the top right, with the triangle drawn inside the circle. Only B shows all of this.

questions.text: Given below are four letterboxes, three of them are written in the same font. Find the one which is written in a different font.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: All four boxes share the digits 1, 2 and 6, so compare those. In A, B and C the 1, 2 and 6 have the same shapes and stroke weights. In D (1265) the digits are narrower and lighter, with a differently shaped 2 and 6, so D is set in a different font.

questions.text: Who is the first Indian to receive an Academy Award (Oscar)?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Bhanu Athaiya won the Academy Award for costume design for Gandhi in 1983, the first Oscar won by an Indian. Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar later, in 1992, A. R. Rahman won in 2009, and M. Night Shyamalan has never won an Oscar.

questions.text: Shown below are four options, each showing consecutive frames representing the movement of a pendulum of an old-style wall clock for an animation movie. Which is the correct option?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A pendulum slows down and stops for an instant at each end of its swing and moves fastest at the bottom. So in equally timed frames the bob positions should bunch up at both ends and spread out in the middle, while the bob moves along an arc. C shows exactly this. A spaces the frames evenly, B also keeps the bob on a straight line, and D bunches the frames in the middle, which is the wrong way round.

questions.text: Match the animals (1, 2, 3, 4) with their respective footprints (P,Q, R, S).
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: A cat walks with its claws pulled in, so its paw print shows pads only (Q). A dog cannot pull its claws in, so its print shows claw marks (P). A horse has a single solid hoof (R) and a cow has a split, two-toed hoof (S). So 1-Q, 2-R, 3-S, 4-P.

questions.text: Identify the final image created if a circular transparent plastic sheet P printed with opaque shapes is folded in the sequence shown below.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Because the sheet is see-through, every shape ends up in the final lower right quarter, mirrored by each fold it goes through. The top half folds down, so the two stars become upside down and the upward triangle becomes a downward one at the upper left. Then the left half folds right, so the dot comes to the top middle and the right-pointing triangle becomes a left-pointing one at the bottom right; the lower left star moves across too. The quarter must show a downward triangle at the upper left, the dot, an upside down star at the top right, another downward triangle in the middle, an upside down star at the lower left and a left-pointing triangle at the bottom right. Only B has this layout with both stars upside down.

questions.text: ChatGPT is an extremely popular artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot from OpenAI. Which of the following options is the correct symbol/logo of ChatGPT?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The ChatGPT (OpenAI) symbol is a knot of six rounded loops that weave over and under each other, and their inner straight parts form a small hexagon in the middle. D shows this. A fills the centre in black, B leaves an open star-shaped gap instead of a hexagon, and C puts a circle in the middle.

questions.text: The word “HOME” was printed on a circular disc and a smaller disc from the center was cut and removed from it. Later, another disc was cut from the smaller disc in the same manner. Find the correct set of discs, if the discs were rotated.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Picture HOME printed across the disc. The outer ring keeps only the ends of the word: the tips of the three arms of E and the outer stem of H with the start of its crossbar. The middle ring keeps the strokes next in from the ends: the right stem of H on one side and the upright spine of E on the opposite side. Both are straight bars, so the middle ring must show a straight bar near its rim on two opposite sides. Only C does. In A, B and D one side of the middle ring shows a curved stroke, which no part of H or E could leave there. So the set is C.

questions.text: P is a completed puzzle made of four-square pieces. If the four pieces are removed to play the puzzle again, which piece shown below will NOT fit into the final image?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: P is made of two kinds of piece: two with a red corner and two with a blue corner, each with part of the white and black swirl. Turn each option to compare. A, B and D can be rotated to match a piece of P exactly. C has its white half-circle on the left with the blue corner at the bottom right, which is a mirror image of the blue piece, so it cannot fit without flipping.

questions.text: A delicious triangular shaped chocolate was left open at night. A mouse could smell the yummy chocolate and could not resist but eat some of it. The remaining chocolate is shown below. How many triangles (including partial) have been eaten?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Extend the two slanted sides until they meet: the full chocolate was a triangle of 9 rows, with 1, 3, 5, ... 17 small triangles, 81 in all. Count the complete triangles still left: 7 + 9 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 56 in the bottom six rows. So 81 minus 56 = 25 triangles were eaten fully or partly: the top three rows (9), and 1, 3, 5 and 7 triangles from the bitten left side of the lower four rows.

questions.text: Closely observe the effect of light and shadow caused by the Sun on the spheres P, Q, R and S. Which is the correct option?

options.label: A
options.text: P =10 am Q = 10:30 am R = 12 noon S = 6 pm

options.label: B
options.text: P = 3 pm Q = 6 am R = 12 noon S = 10:30 am

options.label: C
options.text: P = 9:30 am Q = 3 pm R = 12 noon S = 9 am

options.label: D
options.text: P = 10:30 am Q = 6 pm R =12 noon S = 1 pm

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The shadow falls away from the Sun and is longer when the Sun is low. In India the Sun is in the east in the morning, overhead at noon and in the west in the evening. P is lit from the east with a medium shadow to the west, so it is mid-morning. Q is lit from the west with a very long shadow to the east, so it is evening, about 6 pm. R has a short shadow straight below, so it is noon. S is lit slightly from the west with a short shadow, so it is just after noon. This matches D.

questions.text: The little ones of parents A, B, C, and D were separated by a 2D maze. Only one parent could find its baby. Identify the parent.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Follow each parent's tube from its mouth on the left, staying in the same tube wherever it passes under another, until it comes out on the right. Only the tube from parent B ends at a baby of its own kind, the small blue fish; the other three end at someone else's baby. So the answer is B.

questions.text: What is the total number of capital letter ‘T’ shown in the image below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Scan the picture in narrow strips, left to right and top to bottom, and mark each capital T as you count it, including Ts that are tilted, sideways or upside down. Count a letter at the border only if its T shape is complete, and do not count T-like strokes that belong to another letter such as F, E or a symbol. IIT Bombay's final key gives 16. This is a dense picture: a careful count can easily land one off, which is why the options are 2 apart.

questions.text: If delulu = 010101, skibidi = 0010101, bussin = 010010, and ghosted = 0010010, then what is 010100?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Write each consonant as 0 and each vowel as 1: delulu is d0 e1 l0 u1 l0 u1 = 010101, and skibidi is 0010101. So 010100 is a six-letter word shaped consonant, vowel, consonant, vowel, consonant, consonant. mewing (m e w i n g) is exactly that. boujee gives 011011, pookie 011010 and cheugy 001101 (counting y as a consonant), so none of them fit.

questions.text: Which of the options fits with the black solid figure and makes it a square?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The black figure is a square whose 21 columns hang down to different depths, so the missing white part is 21 bars of different heights standing on the bottom edge. Turn each option a quarter turn so its bars stand up and compare their lengths, column by column. Only C matches every column; A, B and D each have one or two bars of the wrong length.

questions.text: The following images show cave paintings from India. Which of the options is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: P - Ellora, Q - Ajanta, R - Bhimbetka, S - Sittanavasal

options.label: B
options.text: P - Ellora, Q - Ajanta, R - Jhalawar, S - Bhimbetka

options.label: C
options.text: P - Ajanta, Q - Ellora, R - Bhimbetka, S - Sittanavasal

options.label: D
options.text: P - Ajanta, Q - Ellora, R - Jhalawar, S - Bhimbetka

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: P, the graceful princess with fine jewellery, is from Ajanta. Q, the dancing Shiva in red and brown, is from Ellora. R, simple red outlines of animals on rock, is prehistoric Bhimbetka rock art. S, figures among lotus flowers in a pond, is from Sittanavasal in Tamil Nadu. So C.

questions.text: The following image shows a set of letters in different fonts. Which of the options is the word formed by letters of the same font?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Look for the letters that share one style. d, e, l, i, g, h and t are all in the same plain serif type, so delight can be formed. knowing needs the heavy slab k and the black condensed n, pester mixes the sans p with the serif e, and navel mixes the bold n and v with the other letters.

questions.text: P is a transparent glass filled with water as shown below. Q is a white cylinder with parallel lines printed around it. If the cylinder is viewed through the glass from the direction of the arrow, find the correct pattern observed.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The water-filled bowl acts as a lens. In its upper part the bowl's sides are nearly upright, like a cylinder, so the horizontal lines stay almost straight. Near the bottom the bowl curves like a sphere, which bends and squeezes the lines into nested curves. B shows straight lines above and curved loops at the bottom.

questions.text: A toy is made with cardboard and rivets. As shown below, the two car cut-outs are attached on top of the parallel cardboard strips which should move when the child pushes or pulls the horizontal cardboard strip. Different linkage mechanisms are made with cardboard strips (rectangles) and connector pivots (circles). Black circles are fixed pivots (attached to the grey base) and white circles are moving pivots (not attached to the grey base). Which option will show a collision between the two cars?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Each upright strip turns about its black fixed pivot when the horizontal strip pushes its white pivot. If the fixed pivot is above the white pivot, the car on top moves opposite to the push; if the fixed pivot is below, the car moves with the push. In B the left strip has its fixed pivot below and the right strip has it above, so pushing right sends the left car right and the right car left, and they collide. In A both cars move the same way, and in C and D a fixed pivot sits on the moving strip, which locks it.

questions.text: What is the total number of musical instruments in the image below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Sort the instruments by family and count each family separately, ticking each one off: strings (violins, cellos, guitars, mandolin and so on), brass and wind (trumpets, trombones, tuba, French horn, saxophones, clarinet-like pipes), and the rest (triangles, drum, keyboard, grand piano). Watch for instruments partly hidden behind others and for two instruments that share an outline. IIT Bombay's final key gives 27. Like every dense count, a careful count can land one off.

questions.text: Shown below are letters ‘e’ taken from four popular logos, arranged in a sequence. Which of the options is the correct sequence?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The first e is the plain upright e of Reliance. The second is tilted, as in the Google wordmark. The third carries the accent mark of Nestle (written with an e-acute). The fourth is the wide, slanted e of Acer. So Reliance, Google, Nestle, Acer.

questions.text: Shown below are the key frames of a bird flying. Which of the following options is the correct order?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: A wing beat goes from wings fully up, through the downstroke, to wings fully down, and then the wings fold slightly as they come back up. Frame 1 has the wings highest, 4 a little lower, 2 level with the body, 5 fully down, and 3 shows the folded wings rising again. So 1, 4, 2, 5, 3.

questions.text: Shown below is a traditional metal artefact made using the lost-wax casting technique. What is this craft called?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Dokra is the tribal brass casting of central and eastern India made by the lost-wax method, with the spiral wax-thread patterns seen on this deer. Bidriware is silver inlay on blackened metal, Thewa is gold work fused on glass, and filigree is fine twisted wire work.

questions.text: A lever mechanism has Effort (E), Fulcrum (F) and Load (L). For example, a pair of scissors will have an order ‘EFL’ as shown in the image below. Similarly, choose the correct order for a Tweezer and a Nutcracker.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Tweezers are joined at one end (fulcrum), pressed in the middle (effort) and grip at the tips (load), so the order is F E L. A nutcracker is hinged at one end, the nut (load) sits in the middle and the hand presses at the other end, so the order is F L E, the same as E L F read from the other side. Only B gives both.

questions.text: What is the main purpose for the presence of water in a toilet bowl (Western Commode/ Water Closet)?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent back flow of sewer gases.

options.label: B
options.text: To efficiently flush solid, semi-solid fecal matter.

options.label: C
options.text: To regulate water temperature in plumbing lines.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The water standing in the bowl and its bent pipe (the trap) forms a seal that stops gases from the sewer line coming back into the room. It does not do the flushing, control pipe temperature or neutralise acid.
